## Family core-verdict: Core action verdict refusals

Answers: what are core action verdict refusals; why does MetaViewer refuse with these

- Why this family exists: The core is the only authority that admits an input to a capsule. Every proposal gets an `action_verdict/v0.2` reply; a refusal carries exactly one of these reason codes so a caller can tell a refusal (the core said no, nothing was sent) from a failure.
- What the user sees: mvctl or the agent prints the verdict JSON with `"decision":"refused"` and this `reason_code`; the tile shows no input effect.
- How to verify a fix: Repeat the proposal against a fresh `observe` frame; an admitted verdict carries `"decision":"admitted"`. Unit evidence: `cargo test --manifest-path core/Cargo.toml`.

### BUDGET_EXCEEDED

Answers: what does BUDGET_EXCEEDED mean; why do I get BUDGET_EXCEEDED; how to fix BUDGET_EXCEEDED

- Family: core-verdict (also found by: core-reply, adapter-code, ui-host, ui-renderer, tool-code)
- Where raised: `core/src/wire/mod.rs:117`, `agents/metaviewer_agents/_contracts_v02.py:310`, `agents/metaviewer_agents/_contracts_v02.py:2998`, `agents/metaviewer_agents/_contracts_v02.py:3258`, `agents/metaviewer_agents/envelope.py:315`, `agents/metaviewer_agents/export.py:145` and 35 more sites
- Source line: `Self::BudgetExceeded => "BUDGET_EXCEEDED",`
- What it means: The action or capture budget for this surface is spent.
- Why it exists: See the family note above.
- What the user sees: See the family note above.
- Likely causes: Too many proposals or captures inside the budget window; adapter detail `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` also maps here.
- Fix or workaround: Slow down; wait for the budget window, then observe and propose again.
- How to verify: See the family note above.

### STALE_FRAME

Answers: what does STALE_FRAME mean; why do I get STALE_FRAME; how to fix STALE_FRAME

- Family: core-verdict (also found by: core-reply, adapter-code, mw-run, ui-host, ui-renderer, tool-code)
- Where raised: `core/src/wire/mod.rs:114`, `agents/metaviewer_agents/_contracts_v02.py:307`, `agents/metaviewer_agents/_contracts_v02.py:2995`, `agents/metaviewer_agents/_contracts_v02.py:3255`, `agents/metaviewer_agents/envelope.py:314`, `agents/metaviewer_agents/export.py:143` and 32 more sites
- Source line: `Self::StaleFrame => "STALE_FRAME",`
- What it means: The proposal names a frame that is older than (or equal in generation to) the capsule's current frame, or a surface that is unknown.
- Why it exists: See the family note above.
- What the user sees: See the family note above.
- Likely causes: The capsule published a new frame between observe and propose; the agent reused an old frame id; the surface was stopped. See core/src/serve/mod.rs `StaleFrame` arm near the frame generation check.
- Fix or workaround: Observe again and plan against the new frame. Never resend the old proposal.
- How to verify: See the family note above.

- Family: core-verdict (also found by: core-reply, adapter-code, ui-host, ui-renderer, tool-code)
- Where raised: `core/src/wire/mod.rs:115`, `agents/metaviewer_agents/_contracts_v02.py:308`, `agents/metaviewer_agents/_contracts_v02.py:2996`, `agents/metaviewer_agents/_contracts_v02.py:3256`, `agents/metaviewer_agents/envelope.py:314`, `agents/metaviewer_agents/export.py:147` and 28 more sites
- Source line: `Self::SurfaceNotAgentControlled => "SURFACE_NOT_AGENT_CONTROLLED",`
- What it means: The capsule is under human control, so agent input is refused.
- Why it exists: See the family note above.
- What the user sees: See the family note above.
- Likely causes: The tile is in Human mode, or a person pressed Take over. The adapter detail `human control blocks agent input` maps here (core/src/serve/mod.rs `adapter_input_refusal`).
- Fix or workaround: Switch the tile to agent mode or press Release. Switching a Host program between human and agent restarts it [MEASURED].
- How to verify: See the family note above.

## Family core-reply: Core reply and session codes

Answers: what are core reply and session codes; why does MetaViewer refuse with these

- Why this family exists: Codes the core puts on replies and `surface_event` errors (capture, recording, layout, journal, guest commands). They let the UI and tools refuse precisely instead of guessing.
- What the user sees: A `surface_event/v0.2` error or reply with `data.code` set; the UI maps known codes to fixed text and shows others as a refusal.
- How to verify a fix: Repeat the action and confirm the code no longer appears in the reply; for session codes, check `journal-ended.json` in the session directory (see docs/DEBUG.md).

### JOURNAL_FULL

Answers: what does JOURNAL_FULL mean; why do I get JOURNAL_FULL; how to fix JOURNAL_FULL

- Family: core-reply (also found by: ui-host)
- Where raised: `core/src/serve/journal_end.rs:128`, `ui/electron/hostBindings.js:321`, `ui/electron/hostBindings.js:511`, `ui/electron/hostBindings.js:531`, `ui/electron/hostBindings.js:1050`
- Source line: `"data":{"surface_id":"session", "code":"JOURNAL_FULL",`
- What it means: The session journal reached its capacity; admission is closed for this session.
- Why it exists: Every admitted record is journaled before it takes effect, so a full journal cannot accept more work without losing replayability. See docs/JOURNAL_END.md.
- What the user sees: Session text: "Session journal is full. New work is refused (POLICY). Capsules are stopping in order; the accepted journal remains replayable. Start a new session." (core/src/serve/journal_end.rs `journal_full_notice`).
- Likely causes: A long run in one session. A full journal ends the session [MEASURED].
- Fix or workaround: Start a new session; use a fresh session per long run. The old journal still replays with mv-replay.
- How to verify: `journal-ended.json` exists in the session directory; mv-replay on the old journal returns rc 0.

## Family adapter-code: Daemon adapter codes

Answers: what are daemon adapter codes; why does MetaViewer refuse with these

- Why this family exists: The adapter owns the native side of a capsule (containers, displays, identities, network egress). Its codes name which native precondition failed so the core never guesses.
- What the user sees: The code inside an adapter reply detail, in the core log, or on the tile as a refusal.
- How to verify a fix: Repeat the action after the fix; `go test ./...` in daemon-adapter is the unit oracle.

## Family adapter-fault: Adapter faults shown as ADAPTER_* in the UI

Answers: what are adapter faults shown as adapter_* in the ui; why does MetaViewer refuse with these

- Why this family exists: The adapter CLI reports a lowercase fault code and a fixed detail. The Electron host turns it into `ADAPTER_<CODE>` (ui/electron/roleHost.js `surfaceCreateRefusal`), except the codes it maps to named refusals (`binding`, `uncertain`, `profile` with a display pool detail, `identity_unavailable`, `host_program_unavailable`, `host_window_unavailable`).
- What the user sees: Tile or Activity text `ADAPTER_<CODE>: ...`; the main process logs `METAVIEWER_SURFACE_CREATE_REFUSED code=<wire code> detail=<fixed detail or withheld>`.
- How to verify a fix: Add the capsule again; the log line no longer appears and the tile shows a frame.

## Family ui-create: Capsule create refusals in the UI

Answers: what are capsule create refusals in the ui; why does MetaViewer refuse with these

- Why this family exists: Opening a capsule needs a free slot, a profile, an identity, memory and a working surface runtime. Each missing precondition has one code and one fixed sentence.
- What the user sees: The tile or Activity panel shows `<CODE>: <sentence>` (sentence quoted below).
- How to verify a fix: Press Add capsule again after the fix; a new tile appears with a live frame.

## Family mw-run: mw_run refusals (agent runner)

Answers: what are mw_run refusals (agent runner); why does MetaViewer refuse with these

- Why this family exists: mw_run drives a capsule for an agent. It stops with a code instead of guessing whenever it cannot prove identity, frame freshness, input delivery or effect. One static remedy per code is printed to stderr; stdout stays the `metaviewer.mw_run/v1` JSON line.
- What the user sees: A nonzero rc, a JSON result line on stdout with the code, and the remedy sentence below on stderr.
- How to verify a fix: Rerun after the remedy; the result line reports success and rc 0. Unit evidence: `python3 -m unittest tests.test_mw_refusals`.

## Family mw-unregistered: mw_run and tool codes without a registered remedy

Answers: what are mw_run and tool codes without a registered remedy; why does MetaViewer refuse with these

- Why this family exists: Codes raised by tools/ and agents/ that are not keys of the remedy table in agents/metaviewer_agents/mw_refusals.py. They are still refusals.
- What the user sees: If the code reaches the mw_run result line, stderr carries the generic sentence from `refusal_sentence` (agents/metaviewer_agents/mw_refusals.py) for unrecognized codes.
- How to verify a fix: Rerun after fixing the cause named at the raise site.

## Family ui-host: Electron host and packaging codes

Answers: what are electron host and packaging codes; why does MetaViewer refuse with these

- Why this family exists: The Electron main process brokers every call between the renderer, the core and the adapter (roles, terminals, identities, files, wire framing). It refuses with a fixed code rather than forwarding native text to the page.
- What the user sees: A refusal or Activity entry with the code, or a rejected IPC promise in the renderer console; some codes are internal and never shown.
- How to verify a fix: Repeat the action; `npm test` in ui/ is the unit oracle.

## Family ui-renderer: Renderer (wall UI) codes

Answers: what are renderer (wall ui) codes; why does MetaViewer refuse with these

- Why this family exists: Codes the wall UI uses to refuse or explain an action locally (layout, tiles, frames, terminal drawer, intents).
- What the user sees: Tile, header or Activity text; `ERR_*` codes are thrown inside the page and appear in the developer console.
- How to verify a fix: Repeat the action; `npm test` in ui/ is the unit oracle.

## Family tool-code: Tool and agent package codes

Answers: what are tool and agent package codes; why does MetaViewer refuse with these

- Why this family exists: Operator and release tools (identities, ARM64 capsules, demo, packaging, mvctl) refuse with a code before they change state.
- What the user sees: The code on stderr or in the JSON result of the tool, with a nonzero exit status.
- How to verify a fix: Rerun the tool after the fix; its unit test under tests/ is the oracle.

## Family judge: Judge launcher failures

Answers: what are judge launcher failures; why does MetaViewer refuse with these

- Why this family exists: scripts/judge/metaviewer-judge.sh installs and runs the kit. Each failed precondition stops with one code, the problem and the exact fix, and changes nothing after it.
- What the user sees: stderr `<CODE>: <problem> -- fix: <fix>`, exit status 2.
- How to verify a fix: Run the fix, then `bash scripts/judge/metaviewer-judge.sh doctor`; success prints `JUDGE_DOCTOR_OK`.
